subject: Kepler.ai: m9c p95 degradation — provisional fallback authorization request
messages:
From: Afzal Haque <afzal.haque@kepler.ai>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: ops+prod@kepler.ai
Date: 2026-08-04T09:14:00-04:00
Subject: urgent: model m9c p95 jump impacting checkout flow

Team —

Starting ~08:40 UTC we started seeing a significant p95 jump from ~220ms to ~1.2s on requests routed to model m9c (product-search ranking) for our storefront. This is affecting checkout latency for a subset of sessions and has already triggered customer-facing slowdowns (we saw a 3% drop in conversion over the last 20m).

Attached is a small PNG of the p95 trend and a short dump of a representative request (sensitive fields redacted). Can you confirm whether a recent rollout touched m9c or routing rules? Kepler's SLA requires p95 <= 400ms for this endpoint; we are currently outside that bound.

We need an immediate mitigation plan and a request: if there is a safe, proven fallback (previous variant or quantized variant with acceptable accuracy), please advise and proceed with a provisional fallback — we cannot sustain this impact during business hours. Also please log this as an escalation.

Attachments: p95_trend_graph.png

—Afzal
Afzal Haque
Head of Prod Ops, Kepler.ai
afzal.haque@kepler.ai
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Afzal Haque <afzal.haque@kepler.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-04T09:22:00-04:00
Subject: Re: urgent: model m9c p95 jump impacting checkout flow

Afzal —

Thanks for the alert and the trend graph. We're opening an incident channel now and will treat as high priority. 

Immediate asks:
- Ben, Mateo: can you triage and post preliminary hypothesis + ETA?
- Afzal: if you have any representative requests / example inputs that reproduce the long-tail behavior, please drop them to the channel (or attach here).

Provisional plan (need customer greenlight):
1) If rollback to the prior pinned variant (m9c-v1.8) is safe and verified, perform a canary rollback for 10% traffic then full pin.
2) If rollback is not safe, switch to the quantized fallback (m9c-q64) on a provisional basis — note there is a small accuracy delta (expected ~1–3% ranking AUC difference); we'll run targeted checks.

We'll attach a short support digest (support-case-1024.md) with timeline and actions. Kimberly, I'm looping you for authorization to proceed with a provisional fallback and any SLA carveout language we need to surface.

—Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: afzal.haque@kepler.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-04T09:50:00-04:00
Subject: Re: urgent: model m9c p95 jump impacting checkout flow

Quick triage notes (preliminary):
- Correlation with a serving runtime kernel change deployed 2026-08-04T07:30 UTC on the hosted fleet (non-customer-specific optimization).
- Evidence: sudden increase in scheduling wait + KV cache invalidation spikes for longer contexts (requests > 512 tokens).
- Reproduction: I can reproduce a p95 spike locally when enabling the new kernel with a representative request afzal shared (thanks).

Recommendation:
- Trigger rollback threshold: sustained p95 > 700ms for 15 minutes on production traffic for the affected route. We hit 1.2s but need a sustained window to avoid flip-flop.
- Immediate action: canary rollback to m9c-v1.8 for 10% traffic and enable prefix KV caching (this reduces tail). If canary shows p95 <= 350ms after 10m, roll to 100%.
- Alternative: if customers prefer faster mitigation, switch 100% to m9c-q64 (quantized variant) for up to 2 hours while we roll back the kernel change and validate. Accuracy delta expected ~1–3%.

I've attached a small patch diff of the kernel change for reference (kernel-diff.patch) and will start a targeted canary once we get explicit customer authorization.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Afzal Haque <afzal.haque@kepler.ai>
Cc: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-04T10:05:00-04:00
Subject: Authorization request: provisional fallback / SLA carveout for Kepler.ai (m9c)

Afzal —

Appreciate the quick report. We recommend the following mitigation path and need your explicit go/no-go to proceed:

Mitigation plan (summary):
1) Canary rollback to m9c-v1.8 on 10% traffic (ETA 10–12 minutes). Monitor p95 and error rate.
2) If canary is successful, promote to 100% and close the incident.
3) If rollback is not possible (e.g., config drift), we will perform a 100% switch to m9c-q64 for up to 120 minutes while we fix the runtime kernel issue.

SLA / credits note: switching to quantized variant may introduce a small accuracy delta; we will document any user-visible impact. Per our escalation playbook, we will also track the incident for potential SLA credit consideration — please confirm if Kepler would like us to file a formal credit request at incident close.

Please reply with explicit approval to proceed with the canary rollback now, or tell us if you prefer the 100% fallback. Once you reply, Ben and Mateo will execute the plan and post step-by-step updates to the incident channel (link: https://app.redwood.com/alerts/ALRT-7392).

Attachments: rollout-playbook.md

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
